==== src/VerifySample.Tests/ModuleInitializer.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=CommunityToolkitMvvm&min=CommunityToolkitMvvm&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;

// Everything here runs once, when the test assembly loads, before any test.
public static class ModuleInitializer
{
    [ModuleInitializer]
    public static void Initialize()
    {
        // Initializes every Verify.* plugin the project references and has not initialized above.
        // Explicit calls come first so their parameters apply: a plugin can only be initialized once.
        VerifierSettings.InitializePlugins();
    }
}

==== src/VerifySample.Tests/Plugins/CommunityToolkitMvvmTests.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=CommunityToolkitMvvm&min=CommunityToolkitMvvm&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using CommunityToolkit.Mvvm.Input;

// Verify.CommunityToolkit.Mvvm: Serializes a RelayCommand or AsyncRelayCommand as the names of the methods behind it.
// https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.CommunityToolkit.Mvvm
// Note: The method names are read from the private delegate fields, so a command built from a
// lambda snapshots as the generated method name.
// Note: This is most useful alongside a ui plugin: a view model verified on its own otherwise
// hides what its commands do.
public class CommunityToolkitMvvmTests
{
    // A command otherwise serializes as the compiler generated delegate behind it, which says
    // nothing. This writes the Execute and CanExecute method names instead.
    // That makes a view model snapshot show which command was wired to which handler.
    [Fact]
    public Task RelayCommand()
    {
        var command = new RelayCommand(Execute, CanExecute);
        return Verify(command);
    }

    static void Execute()
    {
    }

    static bool CanExecute() =>
        true;
}
